glosses: A dark image projected onto a surface where light (or other radiation) is blocked by the shade of an object.

examples.text: My shadow lengthened as the sun began to set.
The X-ray showed a shadow on his lung.

The stories did not seem to me to touch life. […] They left me with the impression of a well-delivered stereopticon lecture, with characters about as life-like as the shadows on the screen, and whisking on and off, at the mercy of the operator.

glosses: Relative darkness, especially as caused by the interruption of light; gloom; obscurity.

examples.text: I immediately jumped into shadow as I saw them approach.
In secret shadow from the sunny ray, / On a sweet bed of lillies softly layd.
Night's sable shadows from the ocean rise.

glosses: An area protected by an obstacle (likened to an object blocking out sunlight).

examples.text: The mountains block the passage of rain-producing weather systems and cast a "shadow" of dryness behind them.

glosses: A reflected image, as in a mirror or in water.

examples.text: Some there be that ſhadowes kiſſe, / Such haue but a ſhadowes bliſſe.

glosses: That which looms as though a shadow.

examples.text: Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil: for thou art with me; thy rod and thy staff they comfort me.

examples.text: I muſt not haue my boord peſter'd with ſhadowes, / That under other mens protection breake in / Without invitement.

glosses: Unofficial, informal, unauthorized, but acting as though it were.

examples.text: The human resources department has a shadow information technology group without headquarters knowledge.

glosses: Having power or influence, but not widely known or recognized.

examples.text: The director has been giving shadow leadership to the other group's project to ensure its success.

glosses: Part of, or related to, the opposition in government.

examples.text: The shadow cabinet cannot agree on the terms of the agreement due immediately after they are sworn in.

glosses: To shade, cloud, or darken.

examples.text: The artist chose to shadow this corner of the painting.

glosses: To block light or radio transmission from.

examples.text: Looks like that cloud's going to shadow us.

glosses: To secretly or discreetly track or follow another, to keep under surveillance.

examples.text: Soon after departure, we cross the invisible border into Scotland to enjoy more stunning coastal scenery, before the line finally swings inland at Burnmouth to traverse pine-clad valleys, shadowed by the A1 trunk road until we rejoin the coast at Cove, east of Dunbar.

glosses: To represent faintly and imperfectly.

examples.text: Ah, ye admonitions and warnings! why stay ye not when ye come? But rather are ye predictions than warnings, ye shadows!

glosses: To hide; to conceal.

glosses: To make (an identifier, usually a variable) inaccessible by declaring another of the same name within the scope of the first.

examples.text: In this snippet, inside the for loop the a and b variables shadow variables from the outer scope, and while legal, this is almost certainly a programming error.

glosses: To apply the shadowing process to (the contents of ROM).
